flows.desc: One RNR CLI add against the v0.1.0 tag lands the AI Elements items plus RNR's own text/avatar/button/icon into apps/example as editable source; the app then builds, cold-boots on both platforms, and Maestro asserts the seeded header, bubble and green tool badge. The script performs the install and the build, then invokes .maestro/cold-boot.yaml for every on-screen assertion, and finally re-runs it with the fixture removed asserting a NON-ZERO exit — the negative control that makes the whole gate non-fakeable.

A short-name registryDependencies entry (`card` instead of an absolute https URL) resolves against the shadcn WEB registry and installs a DOM component into a React Native app. The build must refuse to emit it. Asserts both halves: buildItem throws on a short name, and every one of the 56 shipped entries resolves to a URL beginning with https:// for both engines.

The post-integration arc: pinned URL to a booting, rendering app on both platforms, end to end in one run. Shares the core flow's script — same install, same build, same Maestro assertions — but excludes step 9, which is an engine self-check on the harness rather than a leg of the developer's journey.

Install into a hostile app, not a clean one: an Expo app that already has its own components/ui/button.tsx with different variants, an npm-latest gesture-handler a major ahead of Expo 57's pin, and no PortalHost in its root layout. Three silent failures, three assertions — the CLI shows what it would overwrite BEFORE writing; expo-doctor fails the pin mismatch rather than letting it surface as a native crash; and the portalling item states PortalHost as an install prerequisite instead of rendering nothing.
